mcat_description.short: Dairy Farming on IndiaMART covers dairy farm shed construction, design, and turnkey infrastructure setup for cow and buffalo milk production operations in India, including stall equipment, milking parlour structures, and ancillary farm buildings.
mcat_description.long: Dairy farm infrastructure in India encompasses the design and construction of cattle housing systems — primarily loose-housing sheds for milking cows and buffaloes — along with ancillary structures such as milking parlours, calf pens, feed stores, chaff cutter sheds, and manure pits. Shed construction follows BIS-recommended layouts adapted to agro-climatic zones, using materials such as cement corrugated roofing sheets (IS 459:1992), RCC flooring, and steel or wooden trusses. Sellers in this MCAT offer a spectrum from individual shed components (roofing sheets, cow cubicles, anti-kick bars, mangers, water troughs) to complete turnkey dairy farm setup services including project reports, layout planning, animal sourcing guidance, and machinery installation. The category is driven by India's growing commercial dairy sector, with small-to-medium farmers and agri-entrepreneurs seeking scalable, cost-effective farm infrastructure for 10–100+ animal units.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, 'Dairy Farming' under the Cattle Sheds taxonomy primarily represents dairy farm shed construction and turnkey infrastructure setup for cow and buffalo milk production. The loose housing system is the BIS-recommended standard for most Indian agro-climatic zones, with layouts prepared for farm sizes ranging from 10 to 100+ animals. Key construction elements include cement corrugated roofing sheets (IS 459:1992), RCC or cement concrete flooring, mangers, water troughs, milking parlours, calf pens, and drainage gutters. The prefabricated and modular shed segment is growing, driven by faster installation times and government incentives for dairy infrastructure. Sellers range from shed construction contractors and prefab structure manufacturers to turnkey dairy consultants offering project reports, layout planning, animal sourcing, and machinery installation. Buyer vocabulary strongly reflects shed design intent ('10 buffalo dairy farm shed design,' 'modern dairy farming setup,' 'cubicles for cow') alongside equipment accessory searches ('adjustable cow anti kick,' 'dairy farm trolley'). The MCAT also attracts misplaced listings for standalone dairy equipment (milking machines, bulk milk coolers) and service listings (farm labour, training) that belong in separate MCATs. India's dairy sector is supported by NABARD financing and state animal husbandry department subsidies, making project report and bankable DPR services a significant sub-segment of buyer enquiries (single source — low confidence for NABARD subsidy claim).
